newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes down with trade a steady seller.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes down with trade a steady seller.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled slightly lower on steady trade selling around 76.00 cents a lb in May delivery, market sources said.
Earlier in the day, speculative buying lifted most-active May to resistance and the high in May of 76.10 cents from this week's low of 73.00 cents.
"At 73.00 cents you will hardly find a farmer in America willing to sell cotton," Smith Barney analyst David Brandon, said. "When the market went up today a lot of farmers turned loose their cotton."
Low prices earlier this week sparked new business which is expected to be reflected in USDA's export and sales report.
"The market came down to a level where we could promote export sales of U.S. cotton," Brandon said, estimating that between 200,000 and 250,000 bales were sold.
USDA put new commitments for the week ended Feb 13 at 166,000 480-lb bales.
May closed 0.03 cent weaker at 75.15 cents, traded 76.10 to 74.75 cents. Spot March ended 0.23 lower at 73.10 cents.
Volume was estimated at 20,000 lots against Thursday's official volume of 20,948 lots.
Open interest in May rose 1,593 lots to 35,555 lots.
